data sources for economic measurement.

::: {.research-item}
## Fiscalité, informalité, transferts et pauvreté en Côte d’Ivoire: une analyse d’incidence sur l’EHCVM 2021

[*With Armand Djaha and N’Dre Lebe*]{.paper-authors}

[**Working paper** · [Read the paper](papers/fiscalite-informalite-transferts-pauvrete-cote-ivoire-2026.pdf) · [Replication code](https://github.com/cae-ins/anstat-microsim)]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract lang="fr"}
*Résumé.* Cette étude mesure l’incidence des impôts et des dépenses publiques
en Côte d’Ivoire à partir de l’EHCVM 2021, dans une analyse *Commitment to
Equity* ancrée sur la consommation par personne. Elle combine barèmes fiscaux,
budgets exécutés et tableau national des ressources et des emplois, en tenant
compte des achats informels. Sous l’hypothèse conditionnelle S3, le Gini passe
de 0,3409 pour le revenu primaire à 0,3167 pour le revenu final. La pauvreté
monétaire atteint toutefois 42,04 % au revenu consommable, contre 37,72 % au
revenu primaire, et 4,35 % de la population devient nouvellement pauvre. Après
valorisation de l’éducation et de la santé publiques, le taux associé au revenu
final tombe à 33,92 %, mais ce coût public n’est pas une ressource monétaire.
Dans une simulation comptable à quantités fixes, une TVA de 9 % sur certaines
ventes finales accroît la pauvreté de 0,47 point sans compensation; le recyclage
intégral de la recette par personne la réduit de 0,22 point.
:::
:::

::: {.research-item}
## Job Quality and Poverty in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire

[**Working paper** · [Read the paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jo8JqBBzvfliCmEQC0UG4NHShR-NiNCe/view?usp=sharing)]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract}
*Abstract.* This study analyzes the influence of household members’ job quality
on household poverty status in Côte d’Ivoire using data from the 2018
Harmonized Survey of Household Living Conditions. Using simple probit
regressions, the study highlights the significant negative effect of a
household head’s job quality on household poverty risk. It also shows that
improving the job quality of other household members reduces the risk of
household poverty. In addition to promoting improved employment conditions for
workers, policymakers should promote women’s access to high-quality jobs. This
could involve investing in social facilities to relieve the burden of caring
for children in the household.
:::
:::

::: {.research-item}
## The Causal Impact of Armed Conflict on Education Outcomes in Mali

[*With Josias Sadia*]{.paper-authors}

[**Working paper** · [Read the paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kvELyRo6ru2XATIfZkzbS5NQ27Km8HPY/view?usp=sharing)]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract}
*Abstract.* This study, using a double-difference methodology and propensity
score matching, analyses the causal impact of Mali’s prolonged crises and
conflicts on the Malian education system. The results indicate that these
events have had a significant and negative impact on education, resulting in a
drop in the average number of years of education between the generations that
attended school during the conflict and the previous generation, ranging from
1.13 to 1.97 years of education. These findings underline the urgency of taking
measures to mitigate these adverse effects and re-establish a functional
education system in the country, highlighting the importance of understanding
the causal impact of the crises on education in Mali.
:::
:::

::: {.research-item}
## Exposure to Violence and Academic Performance Among Adolescents in Côte d’Ivoire

[*With Sekongo Coulibaly*]{.paper-authors}

[**Working paper** · [Read the paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hsOuKR41ZenMkJwZHB-_QiBoDGeIZ5N1/view?usp=sharing)]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract}
*Abstract.* This study analyzes the effects of exposure to violence on the
academic performance of children aged 13 to 18 in Côte d’Ivoire. We examine how
physical, emotional, and sexual abuse affect students’ academic performance
using data from the 2018 Violence Against Children Survey. The results show
that 76.66% of the children in our sample report having experienced at least
one form of violence and display more pronounced academic difficulties than
those not exposed. A binary probit regression indicates that physical and
emotional violence significantly increase the likelihood of school dropout and
grade delay, especially when perpetrated by close adults. Sexual violence does
not show direct effects on academic outcomes in our sample, although it may
lead to indirect consequences.
:::
:::

::: {.research-item}
## Estimating Poverty with Satellite Imagery in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire

[*With Koné Kinin Mamadou, Kouamé Moussa Richard, Koné Djoudori Joachim,
Kouassi Kouamé Aristide, and Doukouré Daouda*]{.paper-authors}

[**Working paper** · [Read the paper](https://gouvci-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/j_migone_stat_plan_gouv_ci/IQCuKg5LwElMSKoG3dK40V69AcFoFGnZSRnBp4MiBgEz0wk?e=tdONmd)]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract}
*Abstract.* This study develops a methodology for estimating poverty in Côte
d’Ivoire using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and deep-learning transfer
techniques. The approach follows a three-stage pipeline: pre-training a VGG16
convolutional neural network on ImageNet, fine-tuning it to predict nighttime
light intensity from daytime imagery, and extracting visual features for
poverty prediction. Using data from the 2018–2019 Harmonized Household Living
Conditions Survey covering 12,992 households, visual features are enriched
with spectral indices including NO₂ concentration, land surface temperature,
and the Enhanced Normalized Difference Impervious Surface Index. The best
model achieves an R² of 40.15%, with predictions remarkably consistent with
survey data: 39.98% predicted versus 39.44% observed in 2018, and 37.86% versus
37.50% in 2021. Temporal validation confirms the approach’s capacity to
capture poverty dynamics, offering a cost-effective complementary tool for
monitoring poverty between survey waves in Sub-Saharan Africa.
:::
:::

::: {.research-item}
## AI Exposure in a Dual Labor Market: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire’s National Employment Survey

[**Work in progress** · August 2026]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-abstract}
This project asks how much of the occupational exposure to artificial
intelligence measured in advanced economies is reachable in a labor market
dominated by informal work. It links GPT and AI Occupational Exposure scores
to Côte d’Ivoire’s National Employment Survey, then combines them with data on
firms’ digital readiness, workers’ reported tasks, and observed AI use. The
analysis distinguishes technical exposure from the exposure that current
infrastructure and local job content make practically reachable.
:::
:::
